title: Wrexham vs. Middlesbrough: Preview, Predictions and Lineups
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Rich FayNov 3, 2026Wrexham drew both of their matches against Middlesbrough last season. / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images (Wrexham), Stu Forster/Getty Images (Middlesbrough)Wrexham face a pivotal week as they look to get their EFL Championship campaign back on track against two of the division’s strongest teams.

The Red Dragons have won just three matches this season, with pressure mounting on manager Phil Parkinson by the week. Wrexham have recorded just one victory in their last five matches and face the unenviable task of hosting Middlesbrough and Wolverhampton Wanderers in the coming days.

Parkinson’s side must show significant signs of improvement if they are to revive their season and ease the pressure on their manager ahead of the November international break. First up is a clash with high-flying Boro, who have already beaten Wrexham in the Carabao Cup this season.

Wrexham have lost striker Sam Smith for a 'significant' period of time / George Wood/Getty ImagesWrexham will be underdogs when they host Middlesbrough in the Championship on Wednesday. Kim Hellberg’s side entered the matchweek at the top of the table, beaten only once in 2026–27.
The Red Dragons still have a cushion above the relegation zone but know that another two defeats this week could leave them in a difficult position heading into the next international break.

Parkinson could certainly do with a shock victory in midweek, but just as important will be a resilient team performance after he questioned the desire of some players following the recent defeat to Sheffield United.

Wrexham will have to find solutions amid the ongoing injury issues. / FotMobParkinson is expected to make changes to his starting lineup, with Max Cleworth likely to return to the defense following his recent recovery from injury. Ben Sheaf could partner Ben Whiteman in central midfield, while George Thomason is pushing for a start at left wing back.
Wrexham have been handed a huge setback following injury to Sam Smith, so Ollie Rathbone and Lewis O'Brien could occupy the attacking midfield roles, with Kieffer Moore at striker.
Wrexham predicted lineup (3-4-1-2): Patterson; Cleworth, Worrall, Doyle; Imray, Whiteman, Sheaf, Thomason; Rathbone, O'Brien; Moore.

Kim Hellberg might not want to change a winning formula. / FotMobHellberg could stick with the same side that defeated Charlton Athletic at the weekend, with little reason to change a winning formula. That would mean Ashley Phillips and Adilson Malanda forming the center-back partnership, with Amario Cozier-Duberry one to watch in midfield.
Lankshear was withdrawn with cramp at the weekend but is expected to be fit enough to start in North Wales if required.
Middlesbrough predicted lineup (4-2-3-1): Vitek; Brittain, Phillips, Malanda, Borges; Berhalter, Morris; Cozier-Duberry, McGree, Conway; Lankshear.
Location: Wrexham, WalesStadium: Racecourse GroundDate: Wednesday, Nov. 4Kickoff time: 2:45 p.m. ET / 11:45 a.m. PT / 7:45 p.m. GMTReferee: Oliver Langford
